content: Albendazole is indicated for the treatment of specific parasitic infections, as detailed below: 1. Neurocysticercosis: Albendazole is prescribed for the treatment of parenchymal neurocysticercosis caused by active lesions due to the larval forms of the pork tapeworm, Taenia solium. Lesions that are considered responsive to albendazole therapy typically appear as non-enhancing cysts without surrounding edema on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) imaging. Clinical studies involving patients with such lesions have demonstrated a reduction in the number of cysts by 74% to 88%. Furthermore, 40% to 70% of patients treated with albendazole showed complete resolution of all active cysts. 2. Hydatid Disease: Albendazole is also indicated for the treatment of cystic hydatid disease affecting the liver, lungs, and peritoneum, which is caused by the larval form of the dog tapeworm, Echinococcus granulosus. This indication is supported by combined clinical studies showing that approximately 80% to 90% of patients who received albendazole for three cycles of therapy (each cycle lasting 28 days) exhibited non-infectious cyst contents. Clinical cure, defined as the disappearance of cysts, was observed in approximately 30% of these patients. Additionally, improvement, defined as a reduction in cyst diameter by at least 25%, was noted in another 40% of patients. Important Note: Surgery is considered the treatment of choice for hydatid disease when it is medically feasible. When albendazole is administered in the preor post-surgical setting, optimal destruction of cyst contents is achieved after three courses of therapy. Additional Note: The efficacy of albendazole in the treatment of alveolar hydatid disease caused by Echinococcus multilocularis has not been clearly established in clinical studies.
